title: A Composition Design Strategy for Refractory High-Entropy Alloys.

recollection.starting_material: (guess) Refractory-element feedstock drawn from Nb, Mo, Ta, W, V, plus ductility/oxidation-tuning additions such as Ti, Zr, Hf, Al, and Cr (typical RHEA pools). Baseline comparisons likely against canonical BCC RHEAs like NbMoTaW or NbMoTaWV.
recollection.intervention: (guess) A composition-design workflow integrating simple thermodynamic/atomic descriptors (VEC, atomic size misfit δ, mixing enthalpy ΔHmix, and Ω parameter) with CALPHAD phase stability screening (and possibly ML/Bayesian optimization) to target single-phase BCC or controlled BCC+B2 microstructures while suppressing Laves/σ phases; incorporation of oxidation/creep constraints and processability filters.
recollection.structure: (guess) Either (i) stable single-phase BCC solid solutions across a targeted temperature window (room temperature to ~1200 C), or (ii) dual-phase BCC matrix with coherent B2 precipitates via Al additions, and minor Cr/Si to form protective scales; minimized Laves/µ/σ intermetallics; refined grains via thermomechanical processing to lock in precipitate distributions.
recollection.mechanism: (guess) Phase stability governed by VEC (favoring BCC at VEC ~4–6) and by ΔHmix/δ to avoid strong negative enthalpy pairs that drive Laves; strength from severe lattice distortion (solid-solution strengthening) and short-range order; additional strengthening from ordered B2 nanoprecipitates; improved oxidation via Al/Cr-enabled continuous Al2O3/Cr2O3 scales; creep resistance from sluggish diffusion and stable precipitates; design map balances strength-ductility by tuning VEC and Al content to control B2 volume fraction and coarsening resistance.
recollection.results: (guess) Demonstration alloys showed: (a) room-temperature 0.2% yield strengths ~1.2–1.8 GPa with 5–10% tensile elongation for BCC+B2 designs, and ~1.0–1.4 GPa with limited ductility for single-phase BCC; (b) retention of high-temperature strength, e.g., 600–800 MPa at 1000 C and >300 MPa at 1200 C; (c) oxidation mass gain reductions by ~50–70% versus NbMoTaW when Cr/Al were included; (d) phase stability without Laves/σ up to ~1100–1200 C by CALPHAD and confirmed by XRD/SEM-EDS; (e) creep rates reduced relative to baseline RHEAs by a factor of ~2–3 at 1000–1100 C. The paper likely presents a composition map and validation on 2–4 alloys to illustrate the strategy.

score.note: The recollection is explicitly speculative and largely describes a different CALPHAD/precipitation/oxidation design study. It only loosely overlaps in mentioning VEC screening and a possible single-phase BCC alloy. It misses the exhaustive Nb-Mo-Ta-V-W composition screening, the selected Nb15Mo2.5Ta40V40W2.5 composition, the reduced-VEC/dislocation-mobility mechanism, and all key measured results; its numerical claims are incorrect.
